hook: Campania's big red grape, Aglianico, made pink by one of the region's classic producers.
pitch: This is a fresh, lively Italian rosé from Campania, made from Aglianico, a southern grape best known for powerful reds. It's our lowest-priced rosé bottle at $70, and it has enough flavour to stand up to tomato, spice and the grill.
taste: Expect a crisp, refreshing pink with red-fruit flavour and a bright, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: Its fresh acidity cuts through the creamy burrata and keeps up with the tomato.
A bright, crisp pink handles the spice and the acidity in the sauce without overpowering the shrimp.
It has enough flavour for the smoky, savoury chicken but stays light and refreshing.

hook: Sangiovese from Chianti Rùfina in Tuscany, the grape that's the backbone of most Tuscan reds.
pitch: This is a fresh, mouth-watering Tuscan red with sour cherry and dried herb flavours and a savoury, earthy finish. It's lively enough to cut through rich pasta and steak, and at $70 it's one of the best-value bottles on our list.
taste: Tangy sour cherry and dried herbs with a savoury, earthy edge, fresh and mouth-watering rather than heavy.

dishes.why: Tuscan red and pasta are a classic match, and the fresh acidity cuts through the rich braised beef while the dried herb notes pick up the herbs in the dish.
Sangiovese is the classic Tuscan wine with grilled steak, and its freshness keeps each bite of rich beef tasting lively.
Sangiovese loves tomato, and its tangy cherry fruit matches the fresh tomato while cutting through the creamy burrata.

hook: The Montepulciano grape here is nothing to do with the Tuscan town. It's grown in the Marche instead.
pitch: This is a dark-fruited Italian red with plum, black cherry and a rustic, earthy edge, plus enough freshness to keep your mouth watering. At $70 a bottle, it's a great-value choice with pasta, chicken or steak.
taste: Dark plum and black cherry with an earthy, rustic edge, a lively freshness and a firm, slightly drying grip like strong tea.

dishes.why: Montepulciano is made for pasta with meat sauce, and its freshness and grip cut through the rich braised beef.
The wine's earthy edge picks up the smoky, earthy flavours of the chicken without overpowering it.
Its dark fruit and firm grip stand up to grilled beef, much as it does with grilled lamb.

hook: Malbec from Mendoza's high-altitude desert, where sunny days and cold nights make it soft and ripe.
pitch: It's a deep, ripe Argentine red with black plum, blackberry and a little hint of violet, smooth rather than harsh. At $70 a bottle it's great value and it's made for a grilled steak.
taste: Dark and juicy, with black plum, blackberry and a floral, violet-like edge, plus a firm, drying grip on the finish.

dishes.why: Grilled beef is Malbec's classic partner in Argentina, and the wine's ripe dark fruit and grip stand up to the rich, savoury steak.
A big, smoky grilled cut to share needs a full red with some grip, and this one brings it at a friendly price.
The soft, ripe fruit suits the rich, slow-braised beef without overpowering the pasta.

hook: Made from the Glera grape in Italy's Veneto, it's the only sparkling wine we pour by the glass.
pitch: It's light and fresh, with lively bubbles and soft pear and apple fruit, so it's an easy, cheerful way to start a meal. At $16 a glass, you can have bubbles without committing to a whole bottle.
taste: Light, frothy and fresh, usually with pear, green apple and a soft, gently fruity finish.

dishes.why: The fresh bubbles cut through the creamy burrata, and the fruit sits nicely with the tomato.
It's light enough not to cover up the delicate raw tuna, and its freshness matches the dish's sharp, salty bite.
Light, cool bubbles calm the spice and refresh your mouth between bites of shrimp.

say: doh-MEN mon-tee-ree-YOOS, lah MOOZ pah-PEE, koht dew ROHN roh-ZAY
hook: A Côtes du Rhône rosé, usually built on Grenache, the grape behind most dry Provençal rosé.
pitch: This is a fresh French rosé from the Rhône Valley, with red berry fruit and a little hint of white pepper. It's easy to enjoy on its own and works well with roast chicken or the trout, and it's one of our most affordable French bottles at $75.
taste: Fresh red berries like strawberry and raspberry, with a light peppery touch and a clean finish.

dishes.why: Grenache loves roast meats, and the red berry fruit is lovely next to the smoky, savoury chicken.
It's fresh and light enough for the delicate trout, and its peppery note picks up the herbs.
The bright berry fruit and freshness cut through the creamy burrata and go well with the tomato.

hook: An Ontario rosé made from Merlot, grown in Niagara, where Lake Ontario softens the climate.
pitch: This is a local rosé from Niagara-on-the-Lake, made from Merlot, so expect soft, plummy fruit with a refreshing, cool-climate lift. It's easy to like, and it's a great pick for anyone who wants to drink something from right here in Ontario.
taste: Expect soft plum and red-berry fruit, smooth and easy, with a fresh finish.

dishes.why: Its soft plummy fruit sits nicely with the smoky, savoury chicken without overpowering it.
Merlot loves mushroom dishes, and the fresh finish cuts the richness of the parfait.
A gentle pink is light enough for the delicate trout but has more fruit than most whites.

hook: Ramato means copper in Italian: this is Pinot Grigio from the Veneto made as an orange wine.
pitch: This is Pinot Grigio from the Veneto made as an orange wine, which means white grapes left in contact with their skins, so it has a copper colour and a little more grip than a usual white. It's crisp and dry with pear and citrus, a fun step beyond everyday Pinot Grigio, and lovely with our tuna carpaccio or shrimp linguine.
taste: Crisp and dry, with pear and citrus, a copper-orange colour and a light grip on the finish from the grape skins.

dishes.why: Its crisp acidity and pear and citrus freshness suit the raw, delicate, salty tuna.
It's fresh enough to match the acidity in the dish, and the light grip stands up to the spice.
The bright acidity cuts through the creamy burrata and keeps the plate feeling fresh.

hook: Grown in the Alps of Alto Adige, where sunny days and cool nights keep it crisp and fresh.
pitch: This is a light, crisp Italian white with gentle pear and citrus and a clean, mouth-watering finish. It's easy to enjoy on its own or with lighter dishes, and at $15 it's our most affordable white by the glass.
taste: Light and clean, with pear and lemony citrus and a fresh, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: It's light and crisp, so it won't cover up the delicate raw tuna, and its freshness keeps pace with the tangy, salty dressing.
Its gentle pear and citrus suit the delicate trout and herbs, much like a squeeze of lemon.
Its crisp freshness cuts through the salty, savoury dressing and keeps each bite tasting clean.

hook: Pinot Nero is Italy's name for Pinot Noir, here from the Veneto, and we pour it by the glass.
pitch: It's a light, fresh red with red cherry and a hint of earthiness, and almost no drying grip, so it's easy to drink on its own. It's one of the few reds that works with fish, and it's lovely with our roast chicken or mushroom parfait.
taste: Light and fresh, with red cherry, a touch of forest-floor earthiness and a soft, smooth finish.

dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic with roast chicken, light enough to let the smoky, savoury flavours lead.
Its earthy side matches the mushrooms and its freshness cuts the creamy richness.
It's a light red with soft tannin, so it can go with fish without tasting metallic or heavy.

hook: A local Niagara Riesling: the cool climate, softened by Lake Ontario, keeps it bright and fresh.
pitch: This is our local white, a Riesling from Niagara, and Riesling usually tastes of lime, green apple and peach, with a lively, mouth-watering freshness. It is light and refreshing, so it is perfect if you want something zesty that wakes up spicy or tangy dishes.
taste: Usually light and zesty, with lime, green apple and peach, and a crisp, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: Riesling is a classic match for spicy food, and its zesty freshness keeps up with the tangy, chili-spiked sauce.
Its bright citrus freshness works like a squeeze of lime over the delicate raw tuna.
Its lively freshness cuts through the creamy burrata and stands up to the tomato and spice.

hook: Sauvignon Blanc from Friuli, cool country between the Alps and the Adriatic, at its best young.
pitch: This is a crisp, zesty Italian white with fresh, grassy, herby notes and a hint of gooseberry and passionfruit. If you like a refreshing white that wakes up fish, salads and shellfish, you'll really enjoy it, and it's great value at $80 a bottle.
taste: Crisp and mouth-watering, with fresh-cut grass, green herbs, gooseberry and a touch of passionfruit.

dishes.why: The wine's fresh acidity and green-herb notes match the trout's delicate, salty, herby flavours.
Raw tuna with a sharp, salty dressing needs a crisp, zesty white that won't swamp it, and this one is exactly that.
Sauvignon Blanc is a classic with shellfish, and its freshness keeps up with the pasta's spice and tang.

say: FAY-oo-dee dee san greh-GOR-ee-oh, GREH-koh dee TOO-foh
hook: Greco di Tufo is one of Campania's three top-tier DOCG wines, from one of the region's classic producers.
pitch: This is a fresh Italian white with a bit more weight than most, with ripe peach, pear and lemon and a firm, mouth-watering finish. It's a great pick for anyone who wants a white with some substance but no heavy oak, and it's lovely with the scallop.
taste: Medium in weight and firm, with ripe peach, pear and lemon and a fresh, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: It has enough weight to match the rich scallop, and its freshness cuts through the richness and lifts the salt.
Its ripe fruit and firm freshness stand up to the spice and tang of the sauce while suiting the sweet shrimp.
Its citrus freshness works like a squeeze of lemon, with enough body for the seared, salty skin.

hook: It's Trebbiano Abruzzese, Abruzzo's own white grape, grown between a warm coast and the cooler Apennine mountains.
pitch: This is a crisp, light Italian white with fresh lemon and green apple and a clean, mouth-watering finish. It's easy to enjoy on its own and brilliant with our lighter dishes, especially the tuna carpaccio and the trout.
taste: Fresh and light in weight, with lemon, green apple and a clean, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: It's light and crisp, so it lifts the delicate raw tuna and its sharp dressing without covering them up.
Its fresh citrus flavour works like a squeeze of lemon over the delicate, salty fish.
Its mouth-watering freshness cuts through the salty, savoury dressing and keeps each bite tasting bright.

say: saint JON boh-soh-LAY roh-ZAY, koht duh TOH, ee-zhay-PAY
hook: Our only rosé by the glass, from the hot, dry Mediterranean Languedoc in southern France.
pitch: This is a fresh, sunny rosé from the south of France, with red berry fruit and a little peppery note. It's our only rosé by the glass, in a 5oz or 8oz pour, so it's perfect if you'd like something pink and refreshing with the burrata or the trout.
taste: Fresh red berries with a soft peppery touch and a clean, refreshing finish.

dishes.why: It's fresh and light enough for the delicate fish, and Grenache rosé goes well with Mediterranean-style herbs.
The red berry fruit and freshness are lovely with the creamy burrata and the tomato.
Grenache suits roast meat, and the fruit is great next to the smoky, savoury chicken.

hook: Garganega is the main grape behind Soave, and it gives gentle almond and citrus blossom notes.
pitch: This is a dry Italian white with soft citrus blossom and a light almond note, fresh without being sharp. It's an easy, food-friendly glass that's lovely with pasta, starters and fish.
taste: Dry and gently fresh, with citrus blossom, lemon and a soft almond note.

dishes.why: The wine's almond note picks up the nutty side of the ravioli, and its freshness lifts the richness.
Soave is a classic match for Italian starters, and its gentle freshness suits the creamy burrata and tomato.
It's light enough to let the delicate, herby trout shine, and Soave is a natural partner for fish.

hook: From Marlborough, where sunny days and cold nights lock in zingy acidity and that cut-grass aroma.
pitch: This is a zesty, dry New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc full of gooseberry, passionfruit and fresh-cut grass. It's bright and mouth-watering, so it wakes up lighter dishes and is easy to enjoy by the glass.
taste: Dry and zingy, with gooseberry, passionfruit and a green note like freshly cut grass.

dishes.why: The wine's zingy freshness matches the tangy, salty dressing and doesn't swamp the delicate raw tuna.
Its grassy, herbal side picks up the herbs on the trout, and the freshness cuts through the seared skin.
The bright acidity refreshes the palate between bites of creamy burrata and juicy tomato.

hook: A Left Bank Bordeaux from the Haut-Médoc, where blends usually lean on Cabernet Sauvignon.
pitch: It's a classic red Bordeaux with blackcurrant and cedar flavours and a firm grip of tannin, the drying feel on your gums. With steak or other rich red meat, the fat softens that grip and the wine turns smooth and generous.
taste: Dark blackcurrant fruit with a cedary, woody edge, fresh and firm with a dry, gripping finish.

dishes.why: Grilled steak is the classic match for Cabernet-led Bordeaux, because the fat in the meat softens the wine's tannin.
The rich, smoky grilled beef makes the tannin taste smooth, and the cedar notes suit the char.
Slow-braised beef is rich enough to tame the grip, and the wine's freshness keeps the dish from feeling heavy.

hook: Tuscany's Sangiovese with Cabernet Sauvignon blended in: savoury cherry with a darker, firmer edge.
pitch: This is a Tuscan red that blends Sangiovese's sour cherry and dried herbs with Cabernet Sauvignon, so it's fresh and savoury with a little more depth. At $87 it's an easy, friendly bottle for pasta, steak or roast chicken.
taste: Sour cherry and dried herbs with a savoury, earthy edge, mouth-watering freshness and a gentle-to-firm drying grip.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant optional, 30 minutes in a decanter (a glass jug) helps it open up

dishes.why: Tuscan reds love pasta, and the wine's freshness cuts through the rich braised beef while its herbal side matches the herbs.
Grilled steak is a classic Tuscan match, and the wine's grip and acidity refresh after every rich bite.
Its savoury, earthy cherry fruit sits nicely with smoky roast chicken without overpowering it.

hook: Barbera from Piedmont, where Barolo comes from: mouth-watering freshness, barely any drying grip, made for food.
pitch: It's a juicy Italian red full of bright red cherry and plum, with a lovely mouth-watering freshness and hardly any of that drying feeling on your gums. It makes rich food taste lighter and keeps you reaching for the next bite, and it's $17 a glass or $91 a bottle.
taste: Bright red cherry and plum, fresh and juicy, with a soft, smooth finish that doesn't dry your mouth out.

dishes.why: The wine's mouth-watering freshness cuts straight through the richness of the steak and the frites, so every bite tastes fresh.
It's soft enough not to overpower the chicken, and the bright cherry fruit sits nicely next to the smoky skin.
The parfait is creamy and rich, and the wine's freshness cleans that richness off your tongue.

hook: It's made from Albarín Blanco, a grape few guests have tried, grown in Tierra de León, Spain.
pitch: This is a light, crisp Spanish white with fresh citrus and green apple, and it leaves your mouth feeling clean and ready for the next bite. If you like Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio but want something a little different, this is a lovely one to discover, and we pour it by the glass.
taste: Expect fresh lemon, green apple and a light herbal edge, with mouth-watering freshness and a clean, dry finish.

dishes.why: The wine's crisp freshness matches the tangy dressing and lets the delicate raw tuna shine.
It's light enough not to cover the fish, and its herbal edge picks up the herbs on the plate.
Its zesty freshness cuts through the creamy dressing and keeps each bite tasting bright.

hook: Same grape and same place as our Brunello: Montalcino Sangiovese, here in its young 2024 form.
pitch: It's a Tuscan red made from Sangiovese, with sour cherry, dried herbs and a savoury, earthy edge, all kept lively by fresh acidity (the mouth-watering tang). You get the grape and place behind Brunello for $95 a bottle, and it's lovely with the beef cheek pasta or the steak.
taste: Tangy sour cherry and dried herbs with a savoury, earthy finish and a gentle grip.

dishes.why: Its fresh tang and herby side cut through the rich braised beef, and Sangiovese is a classic with pasta.
Grilled steak is Tuscany's classic match for Sangiovese, and the gentle grip suits the beef.
Its savoury, earthy edge picks up the smoky, earthy notes of the chicken without overpowering it.

hook: A Sardinian Vermentino, the classic Mediterranean seafood white, usually made in steel to keep it fresh.
pitch: This is a light, crisp white from the island of Sardinia, with citrus, a herbal touch and a faint bitter almond note at the end. It's bright and mouth-watering, so it keeps every bite of fish or seafood tasting fresh.
taste: Light and zesty, with lemony citrus, a hint of fresh herbs and a faint bitter almond finish.

dishes.why: Its citrus and herbal notes pick up the herbs on the trout, and its freshness keeps the delicate fish light.
A crisp seafood white like this cools the spice and matches the tangy, savoury sauce.
It's light enough not to bury the delicate raw tuna, and its zesty acidity matches the dish's tang.

hook: Cannonau is simply what Sardinians call Grenache, and this bottle comes straight from the island.
pitch: It's a warm, friendly red with ripe red berries, a touch of spice and only a gentle drying grip on your gums. It's easy to enjoy on its own and sits beautifully with roast chicken or a rich pasta without ever feeling heavy.
taste: Ripe raspberry and red cherry with a little spice and dried herbs, smooth and warming rather than sharp or heavy.

dishes.why: The ripe red fruit and gentle spice love the smoky, savoury skin, and the soft texture won't overpower the chicken.
It has enough warmth and fruit for the rich braised beef, and its herby side picks up the herbs in the dish.
The spice in the wine meets the spice in the dish, and the soft fruit balances the earthy, creamy flavours.

say: SEH-rah and bar-seh-LOH, ow-kah-LAH, TEH-rah AL-tah
hook: It's a Catalan white from Terra Alta, usually made from Garnacha Blanca, the white version of Grenache.
pitch: This is a fuller, rounder white with ripe pear and stone fruit like apricot, and a gentle herbal touch, so it feels generous rather than sharp. It's a great pick for someone who usually orders red, or who wants a white with enough weight for the roasted chicken.
taste: Expect ripe pear, apricot and a herbal note, with a smooth, rounded feel in the mouth and a dry finish.

dishes.why: It has enough weight to stand up to the smoky, savoury chicken without fighting it.
Its round, ripe fruit suits the rich, sweet scallop and its seared crust.
Its ripe stone fruit and fuller body sit nicely with the sweet, nutty squash.

hook: A Niagara red, usually led by Merlot, from a cool climate softened by Lake Ontario.
pitch: This is a smooth, local Niagara red with plum and a touch of cocoa, softer and rounder than a straight Cabernet. It's an easy bottle to love with the beef cheek pappardelle or anything earthy and savoury, and it's a great way to try Ontario wine.
taste: Ripe plum and cocoa with a hint of chocolate and vanilla, smooth rather than grippy.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes (pour it into a decanter, a glass jug, to let it breathe), optional

dishes.why: Merlot is a classic with pasta in a rich meat sauce, and its soft plum fruit suits the slow-braised beef.
Merlot loves mushroom dishes, and its smooth, cocoa side sits nicely with the earthy, creamy parfait.
Its soft tannin won't overpower the chicken, and the plum fruit works with the smoky, earthy roast.

hook: Vietti, who make our Barolo Monvigliero, also make this white from Piedmont: Arneis.
pitch: This is a dry white from Piedmont, the same corner of Italy as Barolo, made by Vietti, who also make one of the Barolos on our list. Arneis is usually soft and gently rounded, with pear and a light nutty touch, so it's an easy, food-friendly white with richer dishes.
taste: Usually dry and gently rounded, with soft pear and a light nutty, almond-like touch.

dishes.why: Its rounder, softer feel matches the rich, delicate scallop without drowning it.
Its gentle fruit and nutty touch go nicely with the sweet, nutty squash.
A soft, dry white like this sits comfortably beside the creamy burrata and fresh tomato.

hook: Xarel-lo from Penedès, where most Cava comes from, but this one is a white wine without bubbles.
pitch: This is a dry white from Penedès in Catalonia, made from Xarel-lo, a local grape that usually brings lemon, herbs and a mouth-watering freshness. If you enjoy Cava, this comes from the same part of Spain without the bubbles, and it has enough weight to stand up to seafood.
taste: Usually dry and fresh, with lemon, green apple and a herbal edge, and a little more weight in the mouth than a light, simple white.

dishes.why: The wine's fresh, herbal side picks up the herbs on the trout and keeps each bite of the salty skin tasting clean.
It has enough weight for the rich, buttery scallop, while its mouth-watering freshness stops the dish feeling heavy.
Its zesty, lemony character works with the salty, savoury dressing the way a squeeze of lemon would.

hook: A Riesling from Australia's Eden Valley; Riesling's high acidity lets it age for decades.
pitch: This is a crisp, aromatic Australian Riesling with lively citrus and floral notes and a mouth-watering zing. It's refreshing with anything spicy and a great choice for guests who love bright, clean whites.
taste: Bright, crisp and dry, with fresh citrus and floral aromas and a long, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: Aromatic, high-acid Riesling is a classic with spicy food, and it keeps the chilli and tangy sauce feeling fresh.
Its bright freshness cools the spice and cuts through the creamy, earthy flavours.
The crisp acidity lifts the rich, salty sear while letting the delicate scallop shine.

hook: Chablis is Chardonnay from Burgundy's cool climate, and it's one of our by-the-glass whites.
pitch: It's clean and crisp, with fresh citrus and a lean, refreshing finish. It's a lovely glass with seafood if you want something bright rather than heavy.
taste: Clean and crisp, with lemon and fresh citrus and a lean, refreshing finish.

dishes.why: Its crisp freshness lifts the rich, salty scallop and keeps each bite tasting clean.
A lean, citrusy Chardonnay is a natural with white fish and lets the delicate trout shine.
The wine's bright citrus matches the tangy dressing without covering the delicate raw tuna.

hook: Tai is the Veneto name for Friulano, and this 2017 is the oldest white on our list.
pitch: This is a dry, medium-bodied white from the Veneto made from Tai, which is the local name for Friulano, and you can expect pear, almond and a gently bitter, nutty finish. It's a 2017, so it has had several years in bottle, and that gives it a softer, rounder feel than the young whites on the list.
taste: Expect a dry white with ripe pear, almond and white flowers, a smooth, rounded feel and a gently bitter, nutty finish.

dishes.why: The wine's almond, nutty side sits beautifully with the sweet, nutty squash, and it has enough body to match the richness of the pasta.
Its rounded, smooth feel suits the rich, delicate scallop without drowning it out.
It's gentle enough for the delicate fish and has enough fruit to stand up to the salty, herby seasoning.

hook: Lapierre is one of the classic names in Beaujolais, and this is Gamay, good lightly chilled.
pitch: It's a light, juicy red from Beaujolais made from Gamay, full of bright strawberry and cherry, with very little tannin (the drying grip you feel on your gums). It's easy to enjoy on its own or with food, and it's lovely served slightly cool.
taste: Light and juicy, with fresh strawberry and cherry, a smooth finish and almost no drying grip.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic match for Beaujolais, and the light red fruit sits nicely with the smoky skin without covering the meat.
Beaujolais is a natural partner for rich spreads and charcuterie, and the juicy fruit freshens each bite of the creamy, earthy parfait.
It's light enough in body and tannin to drink with a delicate fish, so a guest who wants red with the trout can have one.

say: sha-TOH nair-AK, es-KEES duh nair-AK, soh-TERN
hook: A 2006 Sauternes, nearly twenty years old, and Sauternes is a wine that ages for decades.
pitch: It's a rich, honeyed sweet wine from Sauternes in Bordeaux, with nearly twenty years of age on it. A small 2oz glass is a lovely way to finish the meal, either with dessert or as dessert.
taste: Rich and very sweet, with honey and a smooth, waxy, almost silky feel in the mouth.

dishes.why: The wine's honeyed sweetness matches the rich, nutty pudding, so the wine never tastes sour next to it.
The bright, fresh citrus lifts the rich, honeyed wine, and the wine is sweet enough to keep up with the dessert.
For an adventurous guest, a sweet, rich wine with a creamy, earthy parfait is a classic French way to start a meal.

hook: Real Champagne from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, aged at least 15 months on its yeast.
pitch: This is a true Champagne: dry, crisp and lively, with fine bubbles and a soft, creamy feel from long ageing on its yeast. It wakes up your palate and makes salty, rich starters taste even better, and at $125 it's our friendliest Champagne by the bottle.
taste: Dry and crisp, with fresh citrus, fine bubbles and a smooth, creamy texture from resting on its yeast.

dishes.why: The crisp freshness and bubbles cut through the scallop's richness and love its saltiness.
A light, dry sparkling wine stays delicate next to raw tuna and matches its bright, zesty dressing.
Clean, crisp Champagne suits delicate white fish and lifts the salt and herbs.

hook: It's made from Turbiana, the white grape of Lugana in Lombardy, and you rarely see it on lists.
pitch: This is a dry, crisp Italian white with fresh citrus and orchard-fruit flavours and a clean finish. If you like Pinot Grigio or Chablis but want something a little more interesting, this is a lovely bottle to discover.
taste: Dry and crisp, with lemon and green apple flavours and a fresh, clean finish.

dishes.why: Its crisp freshness suits the delicate, salty, herby trout without covering it up.
The wine's clean crispness balances the richness of the scallop and lets its sweetness come through.
A dry, fresh white keeps up with the citrus and salt on the raw tuna and doesn't overpower it.

hook: Niagara Cabernet Franc: lighter than Cabernet Sauvignon, with red fruit, violets and a hint of green pepper.
pitch: This is a local Ontario red with red berries, a floral touch of violets and a fresh, leafy note like green pepper. It has real flavour without being heavy, so it sits happily alongside roast chicken, mushrooms and herby dishes.
taste: Red berries and violets with a fresh, leafy green-pepper edge and a clean, lively finish.

dishes.why: The wine's red fruit and herby, leafy note suit the smoky, savoury, earthy roast without swamping the chicken.
Cabernet Franc is a classic with charcuterie-style starters, and its freshness lifts the earthy, creamy parfait.
The rich, herbal braise picks up the wine's leafy side, and its lively acidity, meaning the fresh, mouth-watering quality, keeps each bite feeling light.

say: KAH del BOSS-koh, fran-chah-KOR-tah, koo-VAY press-TEEZH BROOT
hook: Ca' del Bosco is a classic Franciacorta house, made like Champagne and aged at least 18 months.
pitch: It's dry and crisp, with fine bubbles and a creamy, lightly toasty depth that feels a step up from Prosecco. If you love Champagne, this is Italy's answer, and it's wonderful with seafood.
taste: Dry and crisp, with fine bubbles, lemon and apple fruit, and a creamy, lightly toasty finish.
serve: 8-10°C · white wine glass or tulip-shaped flute

dishes.why: Its crisp freshness and bubbles cut through the rich, salty scallop, and its creamy side matches the sweet sear.
It's dry and fresh enough for delicate fish, with enough depth to stand up to the crisp seared skin and herbs.
The toasty, creamy notes from ageing suit the earthy mushroom, and the bubbles clean up the richness.

hook: Grüner Veltliner from Alto Adige: think citrus with a white-pepper kick and a savoury, lentil-like note.
pitch: This is a crisp, zesty white with citrus and a little white-pepper spice, plus a savoury edge that makes it more interesting than a simple fruity white. It's lovely with salads, fish and anything with a bit of spice, and it stays fresh right through a meal.
taste: Crisp and zesty, with lemony citrus, a white-pepper tingle and a savoury, almost lentil-like note.

dishes.why: Its crisp freshness cuts through the creamy dressing, and its peppery edge loves the salty toppings.
Its citrus and savoury, peppery notes suit the delicate trout and pick up the herbs.
Its zesty freshness keeps up with the tangy sauce, and its white-pepper note sits happily with the spice.

hook: Niagara Syrah: deep colour, blackberry and black pepper, from a cool climate tempered by Lake Ontario.
pitch: This is a deep, dark Ontario red full of blackberry and black pepper, with a firm grip that loves grilled meat. If you're having the steak or the côte de boeuf, it's a local bottle that really holds its own.
taste: Blackberry and cracked black pepper with a hint of smoke and a firm, drying grip on the finish.

dishes.why: Syrah is made for grilled meat, and its blackberry and smoky notes meet the rich, charred beef head on.
The wine's black pepper picks up the steak's spice, and its tannin stands up to the rich, grilled beef.
Its deep fruit and grip suit the rich, savoury braised beef.

hook: Champagne usually built on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, kept bright and crisp by a cool climate.
pitch: This is a dry, crisp Champagne with fine bubbles and a little more depth from Pinot Noir, a red grape that's usually in the blend. It's elegant enough for a celebration and just as good with mushrooms, fish or roast chicken.
taste: Dry and crisp, with fine bubbles, fresh citrus and a soft hint of red cherry.

dishes.why: The bubbles and crispness cut the creamy richness, and Pinot Noir, usually in the blend, is a classic match for mushrooms.
Pinot Noir is a natural partner for roast chicken, and the freshness keeps each bite lively.
A crisp, dry Champagne suits delicate fish and brightens up the salt and herbs.

hook: A true pink Champagne: non-vintage, so by law it rests at least 12 months on its yeast.
pitch: This is a dry pink Champagne, crisp and fresh with the red-cherry fruit of the Pinot Noir it's usually made with. It's a lovely way to start a meal, and it has enough fruit to carry on through the trout or the roast chicken.
taste: Dry and crisp, with fine bubbles and fresh red-cherry and red-berry fruit.
serve: 8-10°C · white wine glass or tulip glass

dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic match for fish like salmon and trout, and the bubbles keep the delicate, salty fish tasting fresh.
Pinot Noir loves roast chicken, and the red-cherry fruit stands up nicely to the smoky, savoury skin.
Its crisp acidity matches the bright, salty dressing without overpowering the delicate raw tuna.

hook: Nebbiolo, aged by law at least 26 months before release: pale in the glass, but powerful.
pitch: This is Nebbiolo from Barbaresco in Piedmont: pale in the glass but serious in the mouth, with scents of rose petal and tar and a firm, drying grip with lots of freshness. It's built for rich food like our braised beef, and we'll decant it so it opens up for you.
taste: Rose petal and tar on the nose, with a firm, drying grip and mouth-watering freshness, more powerful than its pale colour suggests.

dishes.why: Braised beef and rich pasta are classic matches for Nebbiolo, and the wine's grip and freshness stand up to all that richness.
A big, rich cut of beef softens the wine's firm grip, and the freshness keeps each bite tasting clean.
The richness of the steak tames the wine's drying grip, so the rose and tar flavours come through.

say: zhahn-LOOK koh-lom-BOH, lah BELL duh MAY, san pay-RAY
hook: It's Roussanne from Saint-Péray in the northern Rhône: pear, herbal tea and a touch of honey.

dishes.why: Roussanne is a natural with poultry, and its pear and honey notes love the smoky, savoury chicken.
Its round, rich feel matches the rich scallop while the freshness handles the salt.
Roussanne suits fish with some richness, and its herbal tea notes pick up the trout's herbs.

hook: It's white Burgundy, so it's Chardonnay, from a cool region where each vintage tastes a little different.
pitch: This is white Burgundy, which means Chardonnay from a cool part of France, so it's fresh and clean with citrus fruit and a medium weight in the mouth. It's polished without being heavy, so it's lovely with the roast chicken, the trout or the scallop.
taste: Fresh citrus and green apple with a mouth-watering zing, and a smooth, medium weight that never feels heavy.

dishes.why: Burgundy Chardonnay and roast chicken are a classic match, and its fresh zing keeps the smoky, savoury bird feeling lively.
Chardonnay suits white fish, and its citrus freshness works like a squeeze of lemon on the salty, herby trout.
Its smooth weight sits nicely with the rich scallop while the freshness cuts through the salt.

hook: Chianti Classico carries Italy's DOCG label, its top guaranteed-origin tier; this is Tuscan Sangiovese.
pitch: This is a classic Tuscan red with sour cherry, dried herbs and a savoury, earthy edge, fresh and mouth-watering with a gentle grip. Sangiovese is what Tuscans drink with grilled steak, so it's a lovely bottle to share with our steaks or the beef pasta.
taste: Sour cherry and dried herb with a savoury, earthy edge, fresh acidity and a medium, gently drying grip.

dishes.why: Sangiovese is the Tuscan classic with grilled steak, and its fresh acidity and grip keep the rich, smoky beef tasting lively from first slice to last.
Tuscan red with pasta is a classic, and the dried herb flavour matches the herbs while the acidity cuts the rich braise.
The wine's earthy edge echoes the mushrooms, and its freshness cuts through the creamy richness.

hook: A dry Chenin Blanc from Vouvray in the Loire; 'Sec' on the label means dry.
pitch: This is Chenin Blanc from Vouvray in France's Loire Valley, made dry, with quince, a light touch of honey and really bright, mouth-watering freshness. It has more weight than a simple crisp white, so it's wonderful with our charcoal roasted chicken or the seared scallop.
taste: Dry and very fresh, with quince and a light honeyed note, and a fuller feel than an everyday crisp white.

dishes.why: Chenin Blanc is a classic match for chicken, and its bright acidity and fuller feel hold up to the smoky, savoury bird.
Its freshness cuts the richness of the scallop, while its weight matches the sweet, seared flesh.
The high acidity works like a squeeze of lemon on the delicate, salty trout.

hook: From Ribeira Sacra in Spain's green north-west, usually made from Mencía, a fresh, peppery red grape.
pitch: It's a fresh, lighter red with juicy red cherry, a peppery edge and only a soft drying grip on your gums. If you like Pinot Noir or lighter French reds, this is a lovely Spanish discovery that's brilliant with food.
taste: Juicy red cherry and raspberry with a twist of black pepper and a stony, fresh feel, light on its feet.

dishes.why: Its fresh red fruit and peppery edge suit the smoky, earthy chicken without weighing it down.
The earthy, savoury side of the wine matches the mushrooms, and its freshness cuts through the creamy richness.

hook: Pigato is Liguria's own grape, a close cousin of Vermentino, grown along the Italian Riviera.

dishes.why: Its herby, salty side matches the herbs and salt on the trout, and its texture suits the seared skin.
It's fresh enough for the delicate raw tuna and its salty edge picks up the seasoning.

hook: Masciarelli is one of Abruzzo's classic names, alongside Valentini and Emidio Pepe.
pitch: This is Montepulciano from one of Abruzzo's classic producers: dark plum and black cherry with a rustic, earthy edge, and a firm grip that's made for grilled meat. If you're having the steak or the côte de boeuf, it has the backbone to match.
taste: Dark plum and black cherry with a rustic, earthy edge, a lively freshness and a firm, drying grip on the gums.

dishes.why: Its firm grip and freshness cut through the rich, smoky grilled beef the way Montepulciano does with grilled lamb.
Its dark fruit and earthy edge stand up to the savoury, peppery grilled steak.
Montepulciano is a classic with pasta in meat sauce, and this one has the depth for slow-braised beef.

hook: Sancerre is Sauvignon Blanc from the Loire Valley: a flint-and-citrus style made to drink young.
pitch: It's crisp and zesty, with lemon and lime, a fresh cut-grass smell and a stony, flinty edge. If you like a bright, refreshing white that wakes up seafood and salads, this is the classic.
taste: Zesty citrus, gooseberry and passionfruit, fresh-cut grass and a clean, stony finish.

dishes.why: The wine's grassy, herby freshness picks up the herbs on the trout and its zesty citrus lifts the salty, delicate fish.
Sancerre is a classic with shellfish, and its crisp acidity cuts through the richness of the seared scallop.
The carpaccio is bright and tangy, and a wine this zesty keeps up with it without covering the delicate raw tuna.

say: doh-MEN roh-ZHAY peh-RAN, shah-toh-NUF doo PAHP
hook: Châteauneuf-du-Pape is a named top area of the warm southern Rhône, usually built on Grenache.

hook: It's usually Mencía from Ribeira Sacra in northwest Spain, a region known for steep slopes and fresh reds.

hook: It's a Pauillac, on Bordeaux's gravelly Left Bank, so the blend usually leans to Cabernet Sauvignon.

If you're having steak, it's exactly the kind of red that the fat in the beef softens, so the two make each other taste better.

hook: Nebbiolo from Piedmont, the grape behind Barolo: pale to look at, but full of grip.

Rich, savoury braised beef matches the wine's weight, and its freshness keeps each bite lively.

hook: Left Bank Bordeaux from Saint-Estèphe, where gravel soils usually mean Cabernet Sauvignon leads the blend.
pitch: This is a full, firm red Bordeaux with blackcurrant and cedar, and a drying grip a bit like strong black tea. If you're having beef, it's a classic match: the fat in the meat softens that grip and the wine tastes smoother with every bite.

Slow-braised, rich beef has the weight to stand up to a full red, and the wine's freshness keeps the dish from feeling heavy.

hook: A Lombardy red usually built on Barbera, a grape with very high acidity and gentle tannin.

hook: A red from the Canary Islands, usually Listán Negro, a grape you'll rarely see anywhere else.

hook: Bollinger is one of Champagne's classic houses, named alongside Krug and Veuve Clicquot.

hook: Syrah from Cornas in the Rhône; Terres Brûlées means 'burnt lands', and it tastes peppery.

hook: By law, Barolo ages at least 38 months, 18 of them in wood, before release.

say: SOH-kul BLOSS-er, OR-chard BLOCK, PEE-noh NWAR

hook: From Pauillac on Bordeaux's gravelly Left Bank, where Cabernet Sauvignon usually leads the blend.

Grilled steak is the textbook match for Cabernet-led Bordeaux, because the fat in the meat smooths the tannin.

hook: Pinot Noir from the Burgundy village of Pommard, a red that can even go with fish.

hook: Barolo must be aged at least 38 months before release, with 18 of those in wood.

taste: Pale red with aromas of rose petals and tar, lively mouth-watering freshness and a strong, drying grip on the gums.

The slow-braised beef and herbs meet the wine's earthy, savoury, dried-cherry side, and pasta is a natural partner for Sangiovese.

hook: A Napa Valley Cabernet from 2014: warm days, fog-cooled nights off San Pablo Bay, and years in bottle.
pitch: This is a full, deep Napa Cabernet, with blackcurrant and cedar plus the vanilla and toast that oak (the wooden barrels wine can be aged in) usually brings, and it has had years in bottle to soften its grip. Pour it with the côte de boeuf and the fat in the beef smooths it right out, so it's a true celebration bottle.
taste: Ripe blackcurrant and cedar with hints of vanilla and toast, and with age, notes of tobacco and pencil lead (what wine people call graphite) can creep in.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant about 1 hour (pour it into a decanter, a glass jug, to let it breathe), slowly, leaving any sediment (harmless bits from age) in the bottle

dishes.why: The fat and smoky char of the grilled beef soften the wine's firm tannin, and the blackcurrant fruit stands up to the size of the steak.
Grilled steak is the classic match for Cabernet, because the richness of the meat smooths out the wine's grip.
The rich, savoury braised beef is hearty enough for a full red like this, and the herbs echo its cedar notes.

say: pol zha-boo-LAY eh-NAY, air-mee-TAHZH la sha-PELL
hook: Pure Syrah from Hermitage, a top northern Rhône area whose wines age into smoky, meaty notes.
pitch: This is a deep, dark red with blackberry and black pepper and a firm, drying grip that stands up to big grilled meat. A 2018 has had some years in bottle, and Hermitage is known for turning smoky and meaty as it ages, so it's a real occasion bottle for the côte de boeuf.
taste: Blackberry and black pepper in a deep, dark, firm red that heads towards smoky, meaty notes with age.

dishes.why: Big grilled beef with smoky char is exactly what this deep, peppery Syrah is made for.
The black pepper in the wine matches the spice on the steak, and the grip stands up to the rich meat.
The smoky, savoury chicken picks up the smoky, meaty side Hermitage develops with age.
